capabilities: schedule notes and Anki-style decks for review using FSRS or SM-2
generate multiple-choice questions from notes via AI providers
tutor a single note adaptively through explain-recall-apply sessions
track review statistics with heatmaps, retention and due forecasts
run a Pomodoro timer and manage calendar events
extras: README states there is no telemetry, ads or crash reporting, and everything except AI features works offline; review data is stored centrally rather than in note frontmatter, and the update notes warn users to preserve data.json and describe automatic migration from legacy storage paths.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in spaced repetition or review scheduling, so retaining note content over time requires external tools like Anki or manual tracking.

relations.evidence: turn on Sync with Anki in the background, which needs the AnkiConnect add-on
the way Anki and SuperMemo present cards

requires.name: AI provider API key (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, OpenRouter, Ollama, etc.)
Anki with the AnkiConnect add-on for background deck sync, or a local agent CLI provider

summary: Spaced repetition for notes and Anki-style decks with FSRS or SM-2, plus AI-generated MCQs, an adaptive tutor, a Pomodoro timer and a calendar.
